repos.android-app: React Native Expo, Realm DB local, custom pako-compressed /sync/buffer NestJS sync logic
repos.app-backend: NestJS backend with MongoDB database (Migrated to apps/backend in mono repo)
repos.infra: Docker Compose containing MongoDB, Kong API Gateway, SSL certificates

packages.packages/shared: Exports raw Typescript validation schemas & interfaces directly (removes build steps)
packages.apps/pwa-app: Single Vite SPA supporting tablet PWA (VITE_APP_TARGET=tablet) and web dashboard (VITE_APP_TARGET=dashboard)
packages.apps/backend: Lightweight Fastify server with tsx runtime, direct CouchDB changes feed integration for sequential patient ID generation, Zod validation using shared schemas, and automatic CouchDB CORS setup on boot

database_transition.client: Realm DB -> PouchDB (browser IndexedDB storage) using single VITE_COUCHDB_BASE_URL variable for simple LAN IP target configuration. Includes dynamic seeding of the offline local afiyet_icd10 database (500+ diagnostic entries) and afiyet_custom_entries database to track user-added options (ethnicities, occupations).
database_transition.server: MongoDB -> CouchDB. Backend configures afiyet_patients, afiyet_examinations, afiyet_icd10, and afiyet_custom_entries on startup.
database_transition.replication: Removed manual pako transaction queue sync. Replaced with native PouchDB-to-CouchDB sync (PouchDB.sync live, retry). Support for diagnostic manual resync with overlay toast notifications
database_transition.automatic_server_provisioning: Fastify backend automatically configures CouchDB CORS endpoints (chttpd/cors) on startup using raw boolean and unquoted wildcard values to align with Erlang parser expectations. Docker-compose mounts couchdb.ini at boot to enable chttpd CORS on port 5984 by default.

pwa_offline_constraints.caching: vite-plugin-pwa generateSW, autoUpdate, inline registration for instant offline startup
pwa_offline_constraints.camera: Browser getUserMedia API for taking patient photos (Base64 avatar storage)

client_build_polyfilled_caps.global: Mapped to 'globalThis' in vite.config.ts define block
client_build_polyfilled_caps.events: Installed Node events library and aliased to 'events' to fix pouchdb EventEmitter runtime crashes

test_suites.pwa_tests: Run via 'npm run test:pwa'. Covers offline PouchDB integration tests (initials/birthdate hash-based patient ID generation, schema compliance verification, and successful writes) and form validation tests with RTL/Vitest (obstetric parity-gravida validation, critical vitals range checks, coordinates regex matching).

offline_llm_rag_architecture.client: Vite PWA (apps/pwa-app) compiled via Capacitor/Cordova into an Android APK, running offline inside a WebView.
offline_llm_rag_architecture.sidecar: PocketPal AI sideloaded on the tablet running local HTTP API on localhost:5001 using llama.cpp background native services.

models.embedding: nomic-embed-text.Q4_K_M.gguf (~150MB-200MB RAM) hosted on PocketPal localhost API.
models.llm: llama-3.2-3b-instruct.Q4_K_M.gguf (~2.0GB RAM) hosted on PocketPal localhost API.

rag_database.search_engine: Orama Vector DB restored in-memory client-side inside the WebView from a pre-compiled binary file ('knowledge-base.msp' stored in apps/pwa-app/public/assets/).
rag_database.pre_embedding_pipeline: Node.js builder script inside the monorepo ('packages/rag-builder') that compiles, chunks, and embeds the medical sources at build time using unquantized FP32 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2' (or similar model) on a developer machine, outputting the serialized binary database.

query_ingestion_strategy.method: Sidecar Vectoring (Option 1). PWA compiles patient visit form states and notes into a standardized clinical text string ('Synthetic Query'), calls PocketPal local /v1/embeddings API to get the 384-dimensional vector, and queries the restored Orama database locally.
query_ingestion_strategy.inference: Matched context passages + synthetic query are compiled into a prompt and sent to PocketPal local /v1/chat/completions API using Llama 3.2 3B. The response is streamed to the UI.
